newsitem.title: TURKEY: Turkey's first Iraqi oil cargo has API 35.46.
newsitem.headline: Turkey's first Iraqi oil cargo has API 35.46.

text.p: The first crude oil piped to Turkey's state refinery Tupras from Iraq under a U.N.-approved plan has an API gravity of 35.46 and sulphur content of 1.97 percent, a senior official said on Thursday.
Ergun Kuran, general manager of the company, said in a statement to Reuters that the price of Tupras' oil purchases from Iraq was at "the price fixed for Europe."

Tupras, offered the first contract to be approved by the U.N. to buy from Iraq's limited oil sales, transported 153,000 tonnes of Iraqi oil by tanker last week from Ceyhan terminal in southern Turkey to its western Aliaga refinery.

Kuran said Tupras, which agreed to buy 75,000 barrels per day of Iraqi oil, would transport its future purchases either through "seaway or the pipeline", which is a 447-km link from Ceyhan to its central Anatolian Kirikkale refinery.
"The remaining purchases...will be bought through seaway or the pipeline in the days to come depending on the needs of the refineries," he said.
Tupras, which controls 86 percent of the refinery market in Turkey, runs four refineries -- Aliaga, Izmit, Kirikkale and Batman.
